items.title: Jimmy Cobb — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I remember his name. His name was Mr. Rome. I knew when I saw him, I’d say, awwww.

ctx.x: . . . was not up to date, he wouldn’t let you play. If he came in and saw you, he said, “Come down. Let me see your card.” You didn’t have no card, he say, “Come off the bandstand. You can’t play.” It was really gangster style almost. I mean really. I remember his name. His name was Mr. Rome. I knew when I saw him, I’d say, awwww. If I wasn’t cool, I started to getting off of the bandstand, because he would run everybody. He would go every different club where it was happening. He would show up like the sheriff.
Did you think that the union – was the union a positive force for the musicians, or not?
